settings.observation_operator: H samples fixed exact grid nodes; boundary rows are zero; no interpolation
settings.branch: Zero-start dense Armijo-Newton lower-branch solve, bounds [0.2,3.4]; no fold crossing or branch switching validated
settings.optimizer: Projected gradient with Armijo backtracking; every search direction comes from the discrete adjoint; no state sensitivity in optimization
settings.armijo_condition: L_trial <= L + c*g*(lambda_trial-lambda), using the actual clipped displacement
settings.parameter_error: fitted lambda minus generating continuum truth lambda; includes grid bias for independent data
settings.residual_norms: Unscaled Euclidean primal residual; absolute and relative Euclidean adjoint residual, relative denominator ||H.T W r||2
settings.finite_difference: Central parameter differences; fresh zero-start primal solves at both lambda+epsilon and lambda-epsilon; no state held fixed
settings.reference: Independent objective-only bounded golden section, interval-width tolerance 1e-8; assumes unimodality on the bracket. A sampled landscape is evidence, not a proof.
settings.identifiability: Only fixed interior sensors constrain lambda; projected stationarity or a prior alone is not proof of data identifiability or truth recovery.

same_discrete.definition: Generated once by the same discrete lower-branch forward solver; code-consistency / inverse-crime control only.

observations.continuous_definition: u_alpha(x)=-2 log(cosh(alpha*(x-.5))/cosh(alpha/2)); alpha=1.5; no inverse-grid forward solve used.
observations.perturbation_definition: Fixed deterministic sensor perturbations, used without resampling; not a probability model.

boundary_only_diagnostic.conclusion: Fixed boundary observations carry no information about lambda; fit_parameter rejects this unregularized experiment.

scope: A bounded one-parameter synthetic inverse problem on the tested smooth Bratu lower branch. Same-discrete recovery is an inverse-crime code-consistency control. Independent analytic observations reveal grid bias. Fixed deterministic perturbations are not a statistical noise distribution; no confidence intervals, universal convergence, global identifiability or performance advantage is claimed.
